IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ attributes the balanced alternative to indirect address: one of us is astray and one guided, while God knows the Messenger is guided and his opponents astray; it tactfully says one of us lies.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r2.anchor: فكذبته من وجه هو أحسن من التصريح، كذلك قال الفراء.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r3.claim: The indirect phrasing resembles telling someone who contradicts you that one of us must be lying, while intending him without bluntly naming him.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p166/r3.anchor: وهذا كما تقول للرجل يكذبك ويخالفك: إن أحدنا لكاذب. وأنت تعنيه،

BURHAN:v4p174/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p174/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p174/r4.claim: The verse uses على for guidance and في for error: the guided person is elevated and sees freely, while the misguided person is immersed in darkness.
BURHAN:v4p174/r4.anchor: فاستعملت على في جانب الحق وفي في جانب الباطل لأن صاحب الحق كأنه مستعل

ITQAN:v2p425/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p425/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p425/r2.claim: In 34:24, على for guidance suggests elevation and control of one’s view, while في for error evokes immersion in low darkness and disorientation.
ITQAN:v2p425/r2.anchor: فاستعملت على في جانب الحق وفي في جانب الضلال لأن صاحب الحق كأنه مستعل

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r7.speaker: müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r7.claim: Most commentators say the verse refutes opponents’ claims through an elevated expression that follows the rules of disputation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r7.anchor: yorumlarda ağırlıklı olarak, üstün bir ifade biçimiyle ve münazara (cedel) kuralları içinde muhatapların iddialarının reddedildiği belirtilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r8.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r8.claim: Razi presents the verse as a method for productive debate: admitting either side may be wrong avoids prejudice and lets both reconsider sincerely.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:22/r8.anchor: Râzî ise konuya farklı bir açıdan bakarak şu yorumu yapar: Yüce Allah resûlüne ve müminlere münazara âdâbı

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r6.claim: The question about provision points to God, since the polytheists cannot claim their idols provide for them; Muhammad is told to answer 'God' because they may stay silent out of stubbornness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r6.anchor: ثم رجع إلى خطاب الكفار فسألهم عمن يرزقهم، محتجا عليهم بأن رازقهم هو الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r7.claim: The two alternatives place the monotheists who worship God opposite the polytheists who worship idols and inanimate objects; guidance is a straight way and error is evident confusion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r7.anchor: وإنا: أي الموحدين الرازق العابدين، أو إياكم: المشركين العابدين الأصنام والجمادات. لعلى هدى: أي طريقة مستقيمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r8.claim: The form appears to leave open which side is guided, but in fact God's worshippers are guided and those worshipping others are astray; the indirect formulation shows fairness and gentleness in calling them to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p546/r8.anchor: ومعلوم أن من عبد الله ووحده هو على الهدى، وأن من عبد غيره من جماد أو غيره في ضلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r1.claim: The phrase 'one of us is guided or astray' uses indirectness rather than direct accusation; the Arab saying about the liar among two speakers and the cited poetic examples illustrate the tactic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r1.anchor: وهنا لما سمعوا الترداد بينه وبينهم، ظهر لهم أنه غير جازم أن الحق معه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r2.speaker: حسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r2.claim: Hassan's line is cited as a pointed, indirect challenge: 'You revile him though you are not his equal'; it says the worse of two is a ransom for the better.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r2.anchor: وقال حسان: أتهجوه ولست له بكفؤ ... فشركما لخيركما الفداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r3.claim: The rhetorical device is istidrāj: begin with a point the listener accepts, then move step by step until the truth becomes clear and acceptable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r3.anchor: وهذا النوع يسمى في علم البيان: استدراج المخاطب. يذكر له أمرا يسلمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r4.claim: The argument lets hearers recognize that idols own nothing and neither benefit nor harm; since they are inert, God alone provides and brings benefit or harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r4.anchor: إن آلهتكم لا تملك مثقال ذرة، ولا تنفع ولا تضر، لأنها جماد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r5.claim: Another interpretation sees the wording as belittlement and mockery: God orders Muhammad to rebuke the polytheists indirectly because an oblique accusation can sting more than an explicit one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r5.anchor: وقيل: معنى الجملة استنقاص المشركين والاستهزاء بهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r6.claim: The conjunction aw retains its ordinary alternative force, and the explicit predicate means one of the two sides is on one of the two outcomes without any deletion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r6.anchor: وأو هنا على موضوعها لكونها لأحد الشيئين، أو الأشياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r7.claim: Some grammarians posit an omitted predicate for either the first or second side, supplied by the stated predicate; the author says this deletion is unnecessary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r7.anchor: وقيل: الخبر محذوف، فقيل: خبر لا وله، والتقدير: وإنا لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r8.claim: The example 'Zayd or ʿAmr is in the palace or mosque' shows the meaning is one of these people in one of these places, without supplying an omitted predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p547/r8.anchor: كقولك: زيد أو عمرو في القصر، أو في المسجد، لا يحتاج هذا إلى تقدير حذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r1.claim: The author keeps أو in its ordinary disjunctive sense: each alternative can take a suitable predicate, so no ellipsis is needed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r1.anchor: وإن مع ما يصلح أن يكون خبرا لأن اسمها عطف عليه بأو، والخبر معطوف بأو، فلا يحتاج إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats أو as واو, distributing guidance to one side and error to the other; the author says the ordinary sense suffices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r2.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيدة إلى أن أو بمعنى الواو، فيكون من باب اللف والنشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r3.claim: The preposition على with guidance suggests its possessor stands firm and has mastery over it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r3.anchor: وجاء في الهدى بعلى، لأن صاحبه ذو استعلاء، وتمكن مما هو عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r4.claim: The use of عن with error depicts someone immersed in confusion, unsure where to turn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r4.anchor: وجاء في الضلال بعن لأنه منغمس في حيرة مرتبك فيها لا يدري أين يتوجه

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.claim: Two verses on Iblīs lead into challenges that the Prophet is instructed to put to the disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.anchor: Two verses regarding the nature of Iblīs (vv. 20–21) then segue into a series of challenges the Prophet Muhammad is told to pose to the disbelievers (vv. 22–30).

ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r7.claim: Exegetes take the wording to mean that the speaker is guided and the opponents are clearly astray, though Zajjāj says that is not valid as a literal linguistic construction.
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r7.anchor: وهذا في اللغة غير جائز ولكنه في التفسير يؤول إلى هذا المعنى

ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r8.claim: The wording presents either side as possibly guided or astray; the intended force is that one of two parties is truthful and the other false.
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r8.anchor: إنا لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين أو إنكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r9.claim: He illustrates the indirect formulation with the idiom that one of two people is truthful and one a liar, without naming which.
ZAJJAJ:v4p252/r9.anchor: أحدنا صادق، وأحدنا كاذب، والمعنى أحدنا صادق أو كاذب

THALABI:v8p88/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p88/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p88/r1.claim: One view treats the Prophet's apparent uncertainty about which side is guided as mockery, not doubt; Abu al-Aswad's poem offers a parallel of hypothetical uncertainty despite certainty.
THALABI:v8p88/r1.anchor: وقيل هذا على جهة الاستهزاء بهم وهو غير شاك في دينه

THALABI:v8p88/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p88/r2.speaker: أبو الأسود
THALABI:v8p88/r2.claim: Abu al-Aswad's poem voices uncertainty about loving the Prophet's kin while the source says he was certain that loving them was right.

THALABI:v8p88/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p88/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p88/r3.claim: Another view takes أو as meaning and: the believers are guided and their opponents are plainly astray.

THALABI:v8p88/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p88/r4.speaker: جرير
THALABI:v8p88/r4.claim: Jarir's line supplies poetic evidence that أو can mean واو, joining two names rather than offering an alternative.

RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r1.claim: Many ordinary people worship God chiefly to avert harm or obtain benefit. The preceding verse says none but God can avert harm, and this verse says provision and benefit also come only from Him; the elect worship for His greatness regardless.
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r1.anchor: أن العامة يعبدون الله لا لكونه إلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r2.claim: If the interlocutors do not answer, the Prophet should say that God provides; people acknowledge God as remover of harm in distress but remain heedless of Him in ease.
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r2.anchor: عند الضر ذكر أنهم يقولون الله ويعترفون بالحق

RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r3.claim: The verse teaches a calm method of debate: direct accusations anger opponents and impair reasoning, while admitting that one side is mistaken invites joint examination, avoids stubbornness, and does not lower the Prophet's standing despite his certainty that he is guided.
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#2/r3.anchor: هذا إرشاد من الله لرسوله إلى المناظرات الجارية في العلوم وغيرها

RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r1.claim: Guidance takes ʿalā because the guided person is metaphorically elevated and looking out, while error takes fī because the errant person is submerged in darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r1.anchor: في الهدى كلمة على وفي الضلال كلمة في لأن المهتدي كأنه مرتفع متطلع

RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r2.claim: Error is described as manifest but guidance is not: the straight path to truth is unique, whereas error includes many degrees, some clearer than others.
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r2.anchor: الهدي هو الصراط المستقيم الموصل إلى الحق والضلال خلافه لكن المستقيم واحد

RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r3.claim: Guidance precedes error because it describes the believers identified by we, and they are mentioned first.
RAZI-FULL:v25p222#3/r3.anchor: قدم الهدى على الضلال لأنه كان وصف المؤمنين المذكورين بقوله

STUDYQURAN:34:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r1.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r1.claim: The question implies that there is no creator besides God who provides; provision from heaven alludes to rain and from earth to plants.
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r1.anchor: The question means, “Is there a creator other than God who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?”

STUDYQURAN:34:24/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r2.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r2.claim: The question can also mean: who will provide for you if God withholds His provision?
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r2.anchor: Who is it that will provide for you if He withholds His provision?

STUDYQURAN:34:24/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r3.speaker: IJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r3.claim: Some commentators read aw as “and”: believers are guided, while disbelievers are in manifest error.
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r3.anchor: interpret this verse to mean, “And surely we (the believers) are guided and you (the disbelievers) are in manifest error”

STUDYQURAN:34:24/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r4.speaker: IJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r4.claim: Others retain aw's disjunctive force: either group may be astray or guided, according to the wording.
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r4.anchor: Others maintain that the verse means, “We are astray or guided and you are astray or guided”

STUDYQURAN:34:24/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r5.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r5.claim: The slight ambiguity that disbelievers might perceive in the wording is understood by some as a gentle invitation to embrace faith.
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r5.anchor: The slight ambiguity that disbelievers might see in this verse is then understood by some as a gentle invitation to embrace faith

STUDYQURAN:34:24/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:24/r6.claim: For manifest error, the commentary directs readers to the note on 36:24.

BURSEVI:v7p227/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227/r2.claim: God provides from the sky through rain and from the earth through plants; the question is meant to make polytheists admit their idols control not even an atom and God alone provides.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r2.anchor: {يرزقكم من السماوات} بإنزال المطر {والارض} بإخراج النبات

BURSEVI:v7p227/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227/r3.claim: Because the polytheists hesitate to answer lest they be compelled by the implication, the Prophet is told to state that God is the provider, the only possible answer.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r3.anchor: وحيث كانوا يتلعثمون في الجواب مخافة الإلزام قيل له عليه السلام : {قل الله}

BURSEVI:v7p227/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227/r4.claim: Provision is outward food for bodies or inward knowledge and unveilings for spirits; inward provision is nobler because it yields eternal life, while outward provision gives strength only briefly.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r4.anchor: اعلم أن الرزق قسمان : ظاهر وهو الأقوات والأطعمة المتعلقة بالأبدان وباطن وهو المعارف والمكاشفات المتعلقة بالأرواح

BURSEVI:v7p227/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227/r5.claim: God creates provision and conveys it to both groups, while distributing it more widely or narrowly as He wills.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r5.anchor: والله تعالى هو المتولي لخلق الرزق والمتفضل بالإيصال إلى كلا الفريقين ولكنه يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر

BURSEVI:v7p227/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r6.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p227/r6.claim: A hadith calls seeking lawful livelihood an obligation after the obligations of faith and prayer.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث : "طلب الحلال فريضة بعد الفريضة" أي : فريضة الإيمان والصلاة

BURSEVI:v7p227/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r7.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p227/r7.claim: A hadith says that whoever eats lawful food for forty days will have an illumined heart and springs of wisdom flowing within it.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أكل الحلال أربعين يوما نور الله قلبه وأجرى ينابيع الحكمة في قلبه"

BURSEVI:v7p227/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r8.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p227/r8.claim: A nightly call from an angel at Jerusalem says that prayers, obligatory or voluntary, are not accepted from one who eats unlawful food.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إنملكا على بيت المقدس ينادي كل ليلة من أكل حراما لم يقبل منه صرف

BURSEVI:v7p227/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227/r9.claim: Pure, lawful food clarifies the heart, increases the light of gnosis, and leads to unveilings and spiritual stations.
BURSEVI:v7p227/r9.anchor: ازباكى مطعم وحلالي قوت صفاى دل خيزد واز صفاى دل نور معرفت افزايد

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r1.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r1.claim: Rumi's verses say lawful food yields light, perfection, knowledge, wisdom, love, tenderness, readiness to serve, and resolve for the next life; unlawful food breeds envy, traps, ignorance, and heedlessness.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r1.anchor: علم وحكمت زايد ازلقمه حلال عشق ورقت آيد از لقمه حلال

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r2.claim: The pronoun iya-kum is coordinated with the noun after inna, yielding the sense that either we or you are on guidance or manifest error.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r2.anchor: {أو إياكم} عطف على اسم أن يعني (باشما)

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r3.claim: The competing groups are monotheists worshipping the uniquely providing, inherently powerful God and polytheists worshipping inanimate objects at the lowest level of possibility.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r3.anchor: أي : وأن أحد الفريقين من الذين يوحدون المتوحد بالرزق والقدرة الذاتية

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r4.claim: After the preceding proof, the evenhanded wording silences a stubborn opponent more effectively than directly declaring which side is guided, like a disputant saying one of us is lying.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r4.anchor: وهذا بعد ما سبق من التقرير البليغ الناطق بتعيين من هو على الهدى ومن هو في الضلال أبلغ من التصريح

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r5.claim: Some take aw as waw, yielding: we and you are guided if we believe, or in manifest error if we do not believe.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم أو ههنا بمعنى الواو ، يعني : إنا وإياكم لعلى هدى إن آمنا

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r6.claim: Bursevi prefers aw as deliberate ambiguity displaying fairness, rather than doubt or an attempt to create doubt.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r6.anchor: وأو ههنا لمجرد إبهام وإظهار نصفة لا للشك والتشكيك

BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r7.claim: The different prepositions picture the guided person as elevated and able to see, while the astray person is immersed in darkness, a deep pit, or a dungeon without a way out.
BURSEVI:v7p227#2/r7.anchor: واختلاف الجارين للإيذان بأن الهادي الذي هو صاحب الحق كمن استعلى على مكان مرتفع

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r1.claim: The question points to God’s provision through rain, crops and livelihoods, the sun, moon and stars, and food produced by the earth for people and livestock.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r1.anchor: {قل من يرزقكم من السموات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين}

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r2.claim: The expected answer is initially omitted because the question makes it clear, then supplied as God; if the idolaters say they do not know, Muhammad is to say it.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r2.anchor: وترك الخبر عن جواب القوم استغناء بدلالة الكلام عليه، ثم ذكره، وهو: فإن قالوا: لا ندري، فقل: الذي يرزقكم ذلك الله

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r3.claim: The wording tells the opponents that either the speakers are guided or astray, or the opponents are; one side must be astray.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r3.anchor: يقول: قل لهم: إنا لعلى هدى أو في ضلال، أو أنكم على ضلال أو هدى

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r4.claim: Qatada says Muhammad’s companions told the polytheists that they were not both on one course and one of the two groups was guided.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {قل من يرزقكم من السموات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين} قال: «قد قال ذلك أصحاب محمد للمشركين

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة وزياد
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r5.claim: Ikrima and Ziyad make the implied contrast explicit: we are guided and you are plainly astray.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، وزياد، في قوله: {وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين} [سبأ: 24] قال: «إنا لعلى هدى

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r6.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r6.claim: A Basran grammarian says أو does not express doubt: in ordinary speech, saying one of us struck the other can make clear that the master struck his servant.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r6.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: ليس ذلك لأنه شك، ولكن هذا في كلام العرب على أنه هو المهتدي

TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r7.speaker: آخر منهم
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r7.claim: Another Basran grammarian says Arabs sometimes use أو like the conjunction واو; Jarir’s line means Thalaba and Riyah, supporting an assured but indirect formulation.
TAB-FULL:v19p283#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخر منهم: معنى ذلك: إنا لعلى هدى، وإنكم إياكم في ضلال مبين، لأن العرب تضع أو في موضع واو الموالاة، قال جرير: [البحر الوافر]

TAB-FULL:v19p285/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r1.claim: An anonymous wāfir poem is cited in the same discussion as an example of conditional alternatives phrased so the speaker can state either outcome without conceding error.
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r1.anchor: فإن يكن حبهم رشدا أصبه … ولست بمخطئ إن كان غيا

TAB-FULL:v19p285/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r2.claim: A Kufan grammarian discusses أو as equivalent in sense to واو here, while distinguishing it from free conjunction: in a delegated choice such as one or two dirhams, the listener may take either one or two, but not three.
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r2.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: معنى أو معنى الواو في هذا الموضع في المعنى غير أن القرينة على غير ذلك لا تكون أو بمنزلة الواو

TAB-FULL:v19p285/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r3.claim: The grammarian explains the line as tactful denial: a speaker who knows his opponent lies can say one of us is a liar, and Arab expressions can soften a direct rebuke.
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r3.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: معنى أو معنى الواو في هذا الموضع في المعنى غير أن القرينة على غير ذلك لا تكون أو

TAB-FULL:v19p285/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that God instructs Muhammad to refute the opponents graciously: saying one of us is lying means the interlocutor, not the Prophet himself.
TAB-FULL:v19p285/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي أن ذلك أمر من الله لنبيه بتكذيب من أمره بخطابه بهذا القول بأجمل التكذيب

TABATABAI:34:24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:24/r3.claim: The question about provision challenges the polytheists’ reliance on gods to satisfy them and expand their livelihood: provision is created, and even they recognize that only God creates it, though they will not admit it aloud.
TABATABAI:34:24/r3.anchor: احتجاج آخر على المشركين من جهة الرزق الذي هو الملاك العمدة في اتخاذهم الآلهة

TABATABAI:34:24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:24/r4.claim: Since the opponents will not confess the answer aloud despite inwardly acknowledging it, the Prophet is instructed to answer on their behalf: God provides.
TABATABAI:34:24/r4.anchor: لكنهم يستنكفون عن الاعتراف به بألسنتهم وإن أذعنت به قلوبهم ولذلك أمر أن ينوبهم في الجواب

TABATABAI:34:24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:24/r5.claim: After decisive proof, the Prophet frames the disagreement fairly: one side must be guided and the other clearly astray, so the hearers should judge the evidence and distinguish truth from falsehood.
TABATABAI:34:24/r5.anchor: وهذا القول بعد إلقاء الحجة القاطعة ووضوح الحق في مسألة الألوهية مبني على سلوك طريق الإنصاف

TABATABAI:34:24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:24/r6.claim: The contrast between being on guidance and being in error pictures the guided as elevated at a beacon overlooking the path, while the astray are immersed in darkness without knowing their direction.
TABATABAI:34:24/r6.anchor: أن المهتدي كأنه مستعل على منار

TABRISI:34:23-24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:23-24/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:23-24/r8.claim: The question forces unbelievers to concede that their idols cannot provide for them; the answer is God, who provides from the heavens and earth.
TABRISI:34:23-24/r8.anchor: فإنهم لا يمكنهم أن يقولوا ترزقنا آلهتنا التي نعبدها ثم عند ذلك

TABRISI:34:23-24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:23-24/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:23-24/r9.claim: The either-or wording is fair-minded argument, not doubt: a speaker may say one of us is wrong while knowing who is wrong.
TABRISI:34:23-24/r9.anchor: إنما قال ذلك على وجه الإنصاف في الحجاج دون الشك كما يقول القائل لغيره أحدنا كاذب

TABRISI:34:23-24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:23-24/r10.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
TABRISI:34:23-24/r10.claim: Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali's poem says that if loving the Prophet's family is right, he has attained it; he knows their love is guidance, so the conditional wording is no expression of doubt.
TABRISI:34:23-24/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا يقول أبو الأسود الدؤلي يمدح أهل البيت ع:

TABRISI:34:25/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:25/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:25/r1.claim: One explanation combines both possible claims and leaves reason to distinguish them, effectively saying, I am guided and you are astray.
TABRISI:34:25/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنه جمع بين الخبرين وفوض التمييز إلى العقول

TABRISI:34:25/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:25/r2.speaker: امرؤ القيس
TABRISI:34:25/r2.claim: The poet's pairing of fresh and dried bird hearts with dates illustrates combining alternatives in one expression.

TABRISI:34:25/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:25/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:25/r3.claim: The author calls it an especially effective gentle appeal: the truthful speaker attributes guidance to himself and error to his opponent without bluntly accusing him, prompting reflection.
TABRISI:34:25/r3.anchor: وهذا من أحسن ما ينسب به المحق نفسه إلى الهدى وخصمه إلى الضلال

THALABI:v8p87#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p87#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p87#2/r6.claim: The question-and-answer argument concedes that God provides sustenance from heaven and earth.
THALABI:v8p87#2/r6.anchor: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض قل الله

THALABI:v8p87#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p87#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p87#2/r7.claim: “Either we or you are guided or plainly astray” is a fair-minded form of argument, like saying one of us is lying while knowing which one.
THALABI:v8p87#2/r7.anchor: هذا على جهة الإنصاف في الحجاج كما يقول القائل: أحدنا كاذب وهو يعلم أنه صادق وأن صاحبه كاذب

THALABI:v8p87#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p87#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p87#2/r8.claim: The parties cannot both be on one path: Muhammad and his followers are guided, while those opposing him are astray; the indirect wording refutes them more graciously than direct accusation.
THALABI:v8p87#2/r8.anchor: فالنبي ومن معه على الهدى ومن خالفه في ضلال، فكذبهم بأحسن من تصريح التكذيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r1.claim: The command to say this is addressed to the Meccan disbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi directs readers to the explanation in Yunus and notes that the Meccans already acknowledged God as provider there; this proves that the provider alone deserves worship, unlike idols that provide nothing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r2.anchor: تقدم تفسيره في سورة يونس (¬4). وهذا احتجاج عليهم بأن الله الذي يرزق هو المستحق للعبادة لا غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r3.claim: Since the Meccans could not name any provider besides God, the Prophet is commanded to answer that God is the provider, completing the proof against them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r3.anchor: فثبت الحجة عليهم بقوله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-، # أي: هو الله.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r4.claim: The discourse may split after قل الله: the Meccans ask who provides, the answer ends with God, and then an implicit ثم قل introduces the challenge about guidance and error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r4.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: هذا محمول على أنه لما أمر بقوله: {من يرزقكم} بعد الأمر قل لهم ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r5.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas saying the alif in أو is an added connective in the expression.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r5.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية: الألف صلة للكلام يريد ألف أو (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r6.claim: Al-Nazzam treats أو as coordinated like واو: the two subjects have paired predicates, guidance for us and error for you, as in the night-and-day verse and Imru al-Qays's paired image.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r6.anchor: أو هاهنا بمنزلة واو النسق، وتأويلهما مبتدآن مجموعان لها جوابان مجموعان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda paraphrases the paired meaning as: we are surely guided and you are in clear error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r7.anchor: قول أبي عبيدة قال: معناه # إنا لعلى هدى، وإنكم لفي ضلال مبين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r8.claim: Muqatil says one group is guided—the Prophet and his Companions—while the other, the Meccan disbelievers, is in clear error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r8.anchor: وهو معنى قول مقاتل: نحن وأنتم أمر واحد أن أحد الفريقين لعلى هدى، يعني: النبي نفسه وأصحابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r9.claim: Al-Farra rejects making أو equivalent to واو in Arabic: take one dirham or two permits either one or two, not three as a conjunction reading would imply.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p361#2/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: (معنى " أو" معنى الواو عند المفسرين، والعربية على غير ذلك، لا تكون "أو" بمنزلة الواو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r1.claim: The intended possibilities are that either we are misguided or rightly guided; God knows His Messenger is guided and the others are astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r1.anchor: والمعنى في {وإنا أو إياكم}: إنا لضالون أو مهتدون، وهو تعالى يعلم أن رسوله المهتدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r2.speaker: الكسائي والأخفش والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i, al-Akhfash, and al-Mubarrad say أو expresses no real doubt here: speakers may state that one of two people is wrong while knowing which one, phrasing a rebuke tactfully.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الكسائي والأخفش والمبرد، قالوا: ليس معنى أو هاهنا الشك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r3.speaker: أبو الأسود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r3.claim: Abu al-Aswad's poem about loving Ali says he is not wrong if that love is error; al-Wahidi notes the poet was certain it was not error, using this as a rhetorical argument.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r3.anchor: وأنشدوا لأبي الأسود. يقول الأرذلون بني (¬1) قشير ... طوال الدهر ما ننسى عليا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r4.claim: The phrase directs speech toward the more decorous expression when the truth is known, using a deliberately indirect accusation rather than bluntly calling the other party a liar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r4.anchor: وهو في القرآن وكلام العرب كثير أن يوجه الكلام إلى أحسن مذاهبه إذا عرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says a direct gloss of I am guided and you are astray is not literally valid Arabic, but the phrase resolves to that meaning because the proof identifies which side is guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: في التفسير وأنا على هدى وإنكم إلى ضلال، وهذا في اللغة غير جائز لكنه يؤول إلى هذا المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r6.claim: The surface wording shows an alternative, not actual doubt; exegetes prioritized the intended meaning and therefore treated أو as coordinating like واو.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p363/r6.anchor: وتلخيص الآية: أن أو ظاهرة للشك وليس المعنى على ذلك، والمفسرون راعوا حقيقة المعنى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r1.claim: The provision from the heavens is rain, and that from the earth is vegetation.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r2.claim: God alone provides those things; this question and answer is an argument against the idolaters.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r2.anchor: أي: الذي يفعل ذلك الله، وهذا احتجاج عليهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r3.claim: The wording indirectly challenges them: one side is lying, while the intended charge is that they are astray for associating partners with their Provider.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r3.anchor: وهذا كما تقول لصاحبك إذا كذب: أحدنا كاذب، وتعنيه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r4.claim: The Prophet is told to ask the polytheists who provides for them from the heavens and the earth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r4.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {قل من يرزقكم من السموات والأرض} [سبأ: 24] يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قل للمشركين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r5.claim: The answer to the question of who provides is God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r5.anchor: ثم قال: {قل الله وإنا أو إياكم} [سبأ: 24]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r6.claim: The phrasing says that one of the two groups, the believers or their opponents, is guided and the other plainly astray.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r6.anchor: أي: أن أحد الفريقين نحن وأنتم {لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين} [سبأ: 24]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r7.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r7.claim: Ibn Mujāhid's father says the intended contrast is that we are guided and you are astray; this indirect Arab idiom lets a speaker imply himself as truthful, or his companion as the liar, fitting the Muslims' weakness in Mecca.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه {لعلى هدى} [سبأ: 24] أحد الفريقين، أي: فنحن على الهدى، وأنتم في ضلال مبين، وهي كلمة عربية

BAQILLANI:v1p271/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r1.claim: The author distinguishes pairing, which answers a word or act with a related counterpart, from verbal appropriateness, where related wording recurs in a new sense.
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r1.anchor: وهو على وجهين مزاوجة ومناسبة المزاوجة كقوله تعالى

BAQILLANI:v1p271/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r2.claim: Taṣrīf varies a word across related senses and varies a meaning through different expressions; the author illustrates the former with forms of الملك and the latter with repeated tellings of Moses' story.
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r2.anchor: وأما التصريف فهو تصريف الكلام في المعاني كتصريفه في الدلالات المختلفة كتصريف الملك في معاني الصفات

BAQILLANI:v1p271/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r3.claim: Taḍmīn conveys a meaning without naming it explicitly, either through a word's structure or because the phrase's meaning entails it; this is a form of concision.
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r3.anchor: وأما التضمين فهو حصول معنى فيه من غير ذكره له باسم أو صفة هي عبارة عنه وذلك على وجهين

BAQILLANI:v1p271/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r4.claim: The basmala implicitly teaches beginning actions in God's name, honoring or seeking blessing through it.
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r4.anchor: من باب التضمين لأنه تضمن تعليم الاستفتاح في الأمور باسمه

BAQILLANI:v1p271/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r5.claim: Mubālagha expresses abundance through emphatic word forms such as raḥmān, ghaffār, shakūr, ghafūr, raḥīm, and qadīr, or through broad and extreme expressions.
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r5.anchor: وأما المبالغة فهي الدلالة على كثرة المعنى وذلك على وجوه منها مبالغة في الصفة المبينة لذلك

BAQILLANI:v1p271/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r6.claim: The Quran's formulation, “we or you are on guidance or manifest error,” is listed among examples of rhetorical hyperbole.
BAQILLANI:v1p271/r6.anchor: وكقوله ( ﴿ وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين ﴾ )

BURHAN:v4p208/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p208/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p208/r3.claim: Here أو signals ambiguity: the speaker knows the truth but leaves it unstated to the hearer.
BURHAN:v4p208/r3.anchor: الثاني الابهام وهو إخفاء الامر على السامع مع العلم به

BURHAN:v2p313/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p313/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p313/r1.claim: The intended allocation is that the speakers are guided and their opponents plainly astray; the wording leaves the alternatives open to draw the listener into acknowledging the truth.
BURHAN:v2p313/r1.anchor: والمراد انا على هدى وأنتم في ضلال وانما لم يصرح به لئلا تصير هنا نكته

BURHAN:v2p313/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p313/r2.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v2p313/r2.claim: Al-Sakkaki calls this “the fair address”: placing guidance على and error في pictures the guided person riding freely while the misguided person is immersed in darkness, and tactfully leads the opponent to concede.
BURHAN:v2p313/r2.anchor: ويسمى هذا النوع الخطاب المنصف أي لانه يوجب ان ان ينصف المخاطب اذا رجع إلى نفسه

BURHAN:v3p406/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p406/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p406/r8.claim: The speaker knows he is guided and his opponents are astray, but presents the wording as uncertainty for tactful conciliation and to overcome obstinacy.
BURHAN:v3p406/r8.anchor: وهو يعلم أنه على لهدى وأنهم على الضلال لكنه أخرج الكلام مخرج الشك تقاضيا ومسامحة ولا شك عنده ولا ارتياب

BURHAN:v4p9/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p9/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p9/r1.claim: Yunus argues from facts the audience already admits, then says they will answer “God”; its singular heaven reflects their belief in rain from the visible sky. Saba lacks that prior admission, so the Prophet is told to supply the answer and the plural heavens stress God's varied provision.
BURHAN:v4p9/r1.anchor: السياق في كل منهما مرشد إلى الفرق فإن الآيات التي في يونس سيقت للاحتجاج عليهم بما أقروا به

BURHAN:v4p7/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p7/r2.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p7/r2.claim: Al-Suhayli says the interlocutors admit that rain comes from the clouds, so the singular heaven fits; in Saba the plural addresses their failure to acknowledge what lies above that.
BURHAN:v4p7/r2.anchor: لأن المخاطبين بالإفراد مقرون بأن الرزق ينزل من السحاب وهو سماء

ITQAN:v2p456/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p456/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p456/r2.claim: Aw can leave the matter ambiguous for the listener, as in the deliberately even-handed challenge asking which side is guided and which is plainly astray.
ITQAN:v2p456/r2.anchor: والإبهام على السامع نحو ﴿ وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين ﴾

RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r1.claim: Hyperbole enlarges a meaning by departing from the language's ordinary form; one class uses intensified adjective patterns, such as رحمان from راحم, to express God's all-encompassing mercy.
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r1.anchor: المبالغة هي الدلالة على كبر المعنى على جهة التغيير عن أصل اللغة

RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r2.claim: Other intensified patterns include فعال, فعول, فعيل, مفعل, and مفعال, illustrated by غفار, غفور, قدير, مدعس, and منحار; رحمان is reserved for God because its meaning encompasses all things.
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r2.anchor: ففعلان كرحمان عدل عن راحم للمبالغة

RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r6.claim: A disputant may frame speech as uncertainty to be fair and strengthen the argument: either side may be guided or astray; the conditional claim about a son follows this pattern.
RUMMANI:v1p104#2/r6.anchor: {وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين}

AKHFASH:v2p483#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p483#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p483#2/r3.claim: This is not uncertainty: Arabic presents two sides while meaning that the speaker is guided; a master can say one of us is striking his companion and be understood as the striker.
AKHFASH:v2p483#2/r3.anchor: وقال {وإنآ أو إياكم لعلى هدى} فليس هذا لأنه شك ولكن هذا في كلام العرب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r1.claim: The wording is a tactful challenge: one party is wrong, although each side knows the other is wrong and itself is right.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r1.anchor: {وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين} [هذا] كما تقول: أحدنا على باطل؛ وأنت تعلم أن صاحبك على الباطل، وأنك على الحق.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda paraphrases the phrase directly: you are guided and your group is in manifest error.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p357/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: "معناها إنك لعلى هدى، وإنكم لفي ضلال مبين" (2) .

MAJAZ:v2p148/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p148/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p148/r1.claim: He paraphrases it as we are guided and you are in manifest error; Arabs can use aw where a coordinating wāw joins the paired terms, as in the cited line.
MAJAZ:v2p148/r1.anchor: لأن العرب تضع «أو» فى موضع واو الموالاة

MAJAZ:v2p148/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p148/r2.speaker: قوم
MAJAZ:v2p148/r2.claim: Some say a speaker certain of his own faith uses this balanced wording sarcastically, knowing which side is guided; Abū al-Aswad’s conditional poem illustrates the posture.
MAJAZ:v2p148/r2.anchor: وقال قوم قد يتكلم بهذا من لا يشك فى دينه وقد علموا أنهم على هدى

NAHHAS:v3p345/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p345/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p345/r14.claim: Man is a complete interrogative noun in the nominative as subject, and yarzuqukum is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v3p345/r14.anchor: من في موضع رفع بالابتداء وهي اسم تام لأنها للاستفهام

NAHHAS:v3p345/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p345/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p345/r15.claim: The qāf may assimilate into the kāf, changing the qāf into a kāf.
NAHHAS:v3p345/r15.anchor: ويجوز إدغام القاف في الكاف فتقلب القاف كافا

NAHHAS:v3p345/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p345/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p345/r16.claim: Innā is shortened from innana by deleting one nūn.

NAHHAS:v3p345/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p345/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p345/r17.claim: Iyyākum is coordinated with the subject of inna; coordination by syntactic position would instead use antum and would make guidance apply only to the first group.
NAHHAS:v3p345/r17.anchor: معطوف على اسم إن ولو عطف على الموضع لكان أو أنتم

NAHHAS:v3p345/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p345/r18.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v3p345/r18.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās allows the guidance phrase to apply to the first group; the wording rhetorically presses an opponent to see that one side must be right and the other mistaken.
NAHHAS:v3p345/r18.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون للأول وهو اختيار أبي العباس قال ومعناه معنى قول المستنصر بصاحبه

NAHHAS:v3p345/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p345/r19.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v3p345/r19.claim: The construction resembles saying I will do one thing and you another, and one of us is mistaken, while leaving the listener to recognize which one.
NAHHAS:v3p345/r19.anchor: أحدنا كاذب وقد عرف المعنى وكما تقول أنا أفعل كذا وتفعل أنت كذا

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r1.claim: أو إياكم coordinates with اسم إن.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r1.anchor: قوله: { أو إياكم }: عطف على اسم إن.

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r2.claim: One parse states the first predicate and omits the second; either party may be guided or astray.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r2.anchor: أن الملفوظ به الأول وحذف خبر الثاني للدلالة عليه. أي: وإنا لعلى هدى أو في ضلال، أو إنكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال.

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r3.claim: A second parse reverses which predicate is stated and omitted; the issue is discussed at 9:62.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r3.anchor: والثاني: العكس أي: حذف الأول، والملفوظ به خبر الثاني. وهو خلاف مشهور تقدم تحقيقه عند قوله: والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه [التوبة: 62].

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r4.claim: Neither omitted-predicate parse is literal: the Prophet knows he is guided and unbelievers astray; this is conversational fairness to gain a hearing.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r4.anchor: وهذان الوجهان لا ينبغي أن يحملا على ظاهرهما قطعا؛ لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يشك أنه على هدى ويقين، وأن الكفار على ضلال

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r5.claim: The device is called istidraj: give an interlocutor a premise he accepts so he will listen.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r5.anchor: ويسميه أهل البيان الاستدراج وهو: أن يذكر لمخاطبه أمرا يسلمه، وإن كان بخلاف ما يذكر حتى يصغي إلى ما يلقيه إليه

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r6.claim: An unnamed poetic line about which speaker was worse illustrates the hypothetical formulation.

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r7.speaker: حسان
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r7.claim: Hassan's line about poetic insult and reciprocal ransom illustrates the same device.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r7.anchor: وقول حسان: 3740 أتهجوه ولست له بكفء

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r8.claim: A third analysis treats أو as واو and uses ellipsis and inversion; it is reported from Abu Ubayda.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r8.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكرته منقول عن أبي عبيدة.

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r9.claim: Al-Shaykh keeps the usual alternative sense of أو; one of us is in one of the states, so no predicate is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r9.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وأو هنا على موضوعها لكونها لأحد الشيئين

SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r10.claim: Al-Samin says al-Shaykh gives interpretation rather than parsing; the syntactic account requires ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:34:24/r10.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره هو تفسير معنى لا تفسير إعراب، والناس نظروا إلى تفسير الإعراب فاحتاجوا إلى ما ذكرت

ASAD-NOTES:34:24#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:24#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:24#n35/r1.claim: Asad refers readers to note 49 on 10:31 for the opening question about who provides sustenance.
ASAD-NOTES:34:24#n35/r1.anchor: See note 49 on the first sentence of 10:31.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r3.claim: In 34:24, على presents the guided as elevated and firmly established, whereas في portrays the misguided as fallen or immersed; other verses consistently use these prepositions this way.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r3.anchor: استعمل مع الهداية حرف الاستعلاء (على) ومع الضلال (في)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r4.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf pictures the person with truth riding a fine horse at will, while the misguided person is submerged and lost in darkness.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r4.anchor: لأن صاحب الحق كأنه مستعلٍ على فرس جواد يركضه حيث يشاء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r6.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r6.claim: By contrast, في for error, doubt, and darkness depicts a person immersed and entangled within them.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r6.anchor: الدال على انغماس صاحبه وانقماعه وتدسسه فيه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r7.claim: The path of truth rises with its traveler toward God Most High, whereas the path of error descends with its follower toward the lowest depths.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#7/r7.anchor: فإن طريق الحق تأخذ علواً صاعدة بصاحبها إلى العلي الكبير

HAMASA:v1p202/r1.author: al-Marzūqī
HAMASA:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
HAMASA:v1p202/r1.claim: Al-Marzūqī reads a Banū Asad poet's denial of perfect generosity as modest self-praise and cites 34:24 as a tactful way to present one's own and another's positions.
HAMASA:v1p202/r1.anchor: ومن هذا الباب قوله عز وجل: " وإنا أو وإياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال ". وهذا كلام من نظر لنفسه وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r1.claim: The Prophet is ordered to ask who provides from heaven and earth to corner the polytheists into admitting their idols own nothing, while God alone provides; they do not actually deny this.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r1.anchor: أمر صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقول ذلك تبكيتا للمشركين بحملهم على الإقرار بأن آلهتهم لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السموات ولا في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r2.claim: Because the opponents sometimes faltered to avoid the implication, the Prophet is told to answer God himself; even they have no alternative answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r2.anchor: وحيث كانوا يتلعثمون أحيانا في الجواب مخافة الإلزام قيل له عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r3.claim: The alternatives are one of the two camps: the monotheists, worshipping the sole provider with inherent power, or the idolaters, themselves powerless and sunk to the lowest contingent state; one camp must be guided and the other clearly astray.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r3.anchor: أي وإن أحد الفريقين منا معشر الموحدين المتوحد بالرزق والقدرة الذاتية العابدية وحده عزوجل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r4.claim: This is impartial language: every hearer, ally or opponent, feels fairly addressed; after the preceding proof the audience can infer which side is guided, while indirectness wins the argument more eloquently and with little contention.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r4.anchor: وهذا من الكلام المنصف الذي كل من سمعه من موال أو مناف قال لمن خوطب به : قد أنصفك صاحبك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r5.claim: The phrasing resembles saying, God knows which of us is truthful and which is lying, leaving the listener to draw the conclusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r5.anchor: ونحوه قول الرجل لصاحبه قد علم الله تعالى الصادق مني ومنك وإن أحدنا لكاذب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r6.claim: Al-Alusi cites Hassan's address to Abu Sufyan before his conversion: Do you revile him when you are no match for him? Your worst is ransom for your best; the verse illustrates indirect argument through a fair-sounding alternative.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r6.anchor: ومنه قول حسان يخاطب أبا سفيان بن حرب وكان قد هجا رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r7.claim: Abu al-Aswad's verse about Qushayr and Ali says that if loving Ali is good he gains it, and if it is error he still cannot be mistaken; it gives another example of indirect, tactful argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r7.anchor: وقول أبي الأسود : يقول الأرذلون بنو قشير طوال الدهر لا تنسى عليا بنو عم النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda takes aw as meaning waw, citing a line that breaking bread or breaking a bone is the same; al-Alusi considers this interpretation far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r8.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيدة إلى أن أو بمعنى الواو كما في قوله : سيان كسر رغيفه أو كسر عظم من عظامه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r9.claim: The verse is a formally ordered wrap and spread: on guidance corresponds to we, and in error to you, as reason confirms, like the ordered pairing in Imru al-Qays's image of fresh and dried bird hearts.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r9.anchor: والكلام من باب اللف والنشر المرتب بأن يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r10.claim: The verse is not an instance of dissimulation, despite what some ignorant people claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r10.anchor: وأياما كان فليس هذا من باب التقية في شيء كما يزعمه بعض الجهلة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r11.claim: The apparent syntax needs no ellipsis: the predicate of we or you is the combined alternative, meaning one camp is characterized by one of the two states, as in saying Zayd or Amr is in the market or at home.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r11.anchor: من غير تقدير حذف إذ المعنى إن أحدنا لمتصف بأحد الأمرين كقولك زيد أو عمرو في السوق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r12.claim: Alternative grammatical analyses make the phrase a predicate of inna alone with an omitted predicate for you, or a predicate of you with the predicate of we omitted as recoverable; ayyākum is a detached pronoun after inna was elided.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140/r12.anchor: وقيل : هو خبر ( إنا ) وخبر ( إياكم ) محذوف تقديره لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r1.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r1.claim: Al-Bahr says no ellipsis is needed in this construction, though ellipsis is needed in a phrase such as Zayd or Amr is standing; al-Alusi invites reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r1.anchor: وفي البحر لا حاجة إلى تقدير الحذف في مثل هذا وإنما يحتاج إليه في نحو زيد أو عمرو قائم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r2.claim: Mubin is most naturally an adjective of error, but can describe both guidance and error; after aw, the adjective and pronoun remain singular.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون وصفا له ولهدى والوصف وكذا الضمير يلزم إفراده بعد المعطوف بأو

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r3.claim: Using on for guidance suggests elevation, mastery, and clear vantage, like standing high or riding a horse; using in for error depicts immersion in darkness and a cavern where one cannot find direction, a metaphor by implicit or derived image.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r3.anchor: وأدخل على على الهدى للدلالة على استعلاء صاحبه وتمكنه وإطلاعه على ما يريد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r4.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r4.claim: Ubay's reading is إنّا أو إيّاكم أمّا على هدى أو في ضلال مبين.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p140#2/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي ( إنا أو إياكم أما على هدى أو في ضلال مبين )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r1.claim: The provision from heaven is rain, and the provision from earth is vegetation; if the questioners do not name God, Muhammad is to answer that God provides for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r1.anchor: فالرزق من السموات: المطر، ومن الأرض: النبات، {قل الله} أي:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r2.claim: The wording is fair argument, not doubt: like saying “one of us is lying” while knowing oneself truthful, it conveys that one side is guided and the other astray without an explicit accusation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r2.anchor: ليس هذا على طريق الشك ولكن على جهة الإنصاف في الحجاج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r3.claim: Some take “or” as “and” and the alif as extra, yielding the sense that the Muslims are guided and their opponents astray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p399#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "أو" بمعنى الواو، والألف فيه صلة، كأنه قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r1.claim: The question establishes the point also made in 19:87: the false gods have no power over intercession.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r1.anchor: يريد به تقرير قوله لا يملكون

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r2.claim: There is no other possible answer; silence or hesitation from fear of the implication still signals inward acknowledgment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r2.anchor: إذ لا جواب سواه، وفيه إشعار بأنهم إن سكتوا أو تلعثموا في الجواب

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r3.claim: After the preceding proof identifies the guided and the astray, the wording pretends to fairness—“we or you”—and silences a quarrelsome opponent more effectively than direct accusation; it is not real uncertainty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r3.anchor: وهو بعد ما تقدم من التقرير البليغ الدال على من هو على الهدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r4.claim: The two groups are monotheists who worship the sole giver of provision and possessor of intrinsic power, and idolaters who associate lowly inanimate beings with Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r4.anchor: والمشركين به الجماد النازل في أدنى المراتب الإمكانية

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r5.claim: The poet Ḥassān offers a parallel in which a seemingly evenhanded question carries a pointed rebuke: “Which of you is the lesser, let the better of you be ransomed.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r5.anchor:
ونظيره قول حسان:
أتهجوه ولست له بكفء

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r6.claim: The preposition ʿalā evokes a guided person above a minaret surveying things or riding a horse he can direct.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r6.anchor: لأن الهادي كمن صعد منارا ينظر الأشياء ويتطلع عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r7.claim: The preposition fī evokes a lost person immersed in darkness and confusion, or confined in a pit with no escape.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:24/r7.anchor: والضال كأنه منغمس في ظلام مرتبك لا يرى شيئا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r1.claim: Because all sustenance depends on the two realms and the question is a reminder and rebuke, God names the heavens in the plural but earth in the singular, since they know no other earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r1.anchor: كل شيء من الرزق متوقفا على الكونين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r2.claim: They already acknowledge God alone provides sustenance, but this confession has not led them to exclusive worship; the commanded answer confronts them as if they denied it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r2.anchor: ولما كان من المعلوم أنهم مقرون بأن ذلك لله وحده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r3.claim: Saying “God” after the question is the plain conclusion of the proof and exposes the inconsistency between their admission and their worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r3.anchor: قل الله } أي الملك الأعلى وحده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r4.claim: The disjunctive “or” is not “and”: one party must be on one of two still-unspecified states, guidance or error, a fair challenge that urges careful, unbiased judgment because the stakes are grave.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r4.anchor: أي إن أحد فريقينا على إحدى الحالتين مبهمة غير معنية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r5.speaker: ابن الجوزي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī compares this indirect challenge to telling someone known to be lying that one of us is a liar, or telling a false report’s listener to say “if God wills.”
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r5.anchor: قال ابن الجوزي : وهذا كما تقول للرجال تكذبه : والله إن أحدنا لكاذب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r6.claim: The guided are compared to riders who can direct their mount where they wish.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p177/r6.anchor: ثم مثل المهتدين بمن هو على متن جواد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r1.claim: Guidance is like riding above a mount: one follows what is right and can see and avoid anything that might lead to error.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r1.anchor: في متابعة ما ينبغي أن يعمل مستعلين عليه ناظرين لكل ما يمكن أن يعرض فيه مما قد يجر إلى ضلال فتنكبه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r2.claim: Error is immersion in mistaken belief about the truth, surrounding its subject so completely that he cannot reach a correct view.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r2.anchor: عن الحق في الاعتقاد المناسب فيه منغمسين فيه وهو محيط بالمبتلى به لا يتمكن معه من وجه صواب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r3.claim: Manifest error is clear and calls others to recognize it, but the person immersed in it cannot perceive his condition until he steps outside it and sees his conduct lacked reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r3.anchor: فإنه لا يحس بنفسه وما بينه وبين أن يستبصر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r4.claim: The inclusive challenge urges examination of evidence they had refused, such as their saying that their hearts were covered; it is unusually fair because the speaker includes himself among those who might be right or wrong.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r4.anchor: ففي هذا حث على النظر الذي كانوا يأبونه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r5.speaker: خالد بن الوليد وعمرو بن العاص
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r5.claim: Khalid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said they had once been astonished when anyone entered Islam, but now were astonished when anyone hesitated about it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r5.anchor: كخالد بن الوليد وعمرو بن العاص

DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says God then commanded the Prophet to ask people who provides for them from the heavens and earth.
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: ثم أمره الله أن يسأل الناس فقال {قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض}

DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r9.claim: Ikrima reads the deliberately framed alternatives as an assertion: the believers are guided and the addressees are clearly astray.
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين} قال {إنا} نحن لعلى هدى وانكم في ضلال مبين

DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r10.claim: Qatada says Muhammad’s Companions used this formulation with polytheists to make clear that the two parties were not on one course and one party was guided.
DURR-FULL:v6p700#2/r10.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإنا أو إياكم} قال: قد قال ذلك أصحاب محمد للمشركين والله ما نحن وأنتم على أمر واحد ان أحد الفريقين مهتد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r1.claim: The argument shifts from idols’ failure to help in this life and the next to their unworthiness of worship: only the provider deserves thanks, and acknowledging God as provider entails His unique divinity, which cannot be divided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r1.anchor: انتقال من دمغ المشركين بضعف آلهتهم وانتفاء جدواها عليهم في الدنيا والآخرة إلى إلزامهم بطلان عبادتها بأنها لا تستحق العبادة لأن مستحق العبادة هو الذي يرزق عباده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r2.claim: Repeating the command ‘say’ heightens attention to the statement, since the original command already signals the importance of public proclamation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r2.anchor: وأعيد الأمر بالقول لزيادة الاهتمام بالمقول فإن أصل الأمر بالقول في مقام التصدي للتبليغ دال على الاهتمام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r3.claim: The question prompts recognition of the error; ‘God’ is supplied as the questioners’ answer because they would not deny it, as in the parallel question in Yunus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r3.anchor: و { من } استفهام للتنبيه على الخطأ ولذلك أعقب بالجواب من طرف السائل بقوله : { قل الله } لتحقق أنهم لا ينكرون ذلك الجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r4.claim: The opening question has a similar precedent in Surat al-Raʿd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r4.anchor: وتقدم نظير صدر هذه الآية في سورة الرعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r5.claim: By setting the teams’ opposed states as guidance or manifest error, ‘or’ presents an exhaustive dilemma in a seemingly open-handed way that traps the opponent in the argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r5.anchor: وعطف على الاستفهام إبراز المقصد بطريقة خفية توقع الخصم في شرك المغلوبية وذلك بترديد حالتي الفريقين بين حالة هدى وحالة ضلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r6.claim: The word ‘or’ conveys alternatives taken from doubt: because each side opposes the other in truth or its absence, their states must be one of these two.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r6.anchor: ولذلك جيء بحرف أو } المفيد للترديد المنتزع من الشك . وهذا اللون من الكلام يسمى الكلام المنصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r7.claim: This ‘fair’ debating style, called irkhaʾ al-ʿinan, grants the opponent room without provoking anger, though the context clearly establishes the proof against them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r7.anchor: وهذا اللون من الكلام يسمى الكلام المنصف وهو أن لا يترك المجادل لخصمه موجب تغيظ واحتداد في الجدال ، ويسمى في علم المناظرة إرخاء العنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r8.claim: The ordered pairing of ‘we’ with guidance and ‘you’ with error indirectly signals which side is right through ordered wrap-and-distribution; this allusion is more effective than explicit accusation in winning over an opponent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p191/r8.anchor: ومن لطائفه هنا أن اشتمل على إيماء إلى ترجيح أحد الجانبين في أحد الاحتمالين بطريق مقابلة الجانبين في ترتيب الحالتين باللف والنشر المرتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r1.claim: Prophetic explanations sometimes draw on a possible sense beyond the construction’s primary meaning, awakening listeners to the full range of meanings Quranic wording can bear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r1.anchor: أنه ليس هو المعنى الأسبق من التركيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r8.claim: The Prophet’s prostrations at Quranic prostration passages may reflect this principle of drawing out a possible meaning; if revealed, they provide stronger evidence that God intends meanings the wording can bear without opposing its aims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r8.anchor: وما أرى سجود النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مواضع سجود التلاوة من القرآن إلا راجعا إلى هذا الأصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r1.claim: The question about provision from heaven and earth is an argument; the Prophet is told to answer Allah because opponents are stunned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى نبيه على جهة الاحتجاج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r2.claim: For an obvious question, state the answer briefly and move to the next proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r2.anchor: وهذه السبيل في كل سؤال جوابه في غاية الوضوح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r3.claim: “We or you” softens the invitation and prompts reflection, like telling an opponent one of you must be wrong; the addressees are implied to be astray.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وإنا أو إياكم تلطف في الدعوة والمحاورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r4.claim: One of the two predicates is omitted because the remaining predicate signals it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r4.anchor: وحذف أحد الخبرين لدلالة الباقي عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda takes aw as “and,” yielding “we and you are on guidance or error,” with two predicates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أو في الآية بمعنى واو النسق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects Abu Ubayda’s parsing as unsupported by the wording, though both analyses put guidance with believers and error with unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r6.anchor: وهذا القول غير متجه واللفظ لا يساعده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r1.claim: The provision from heaven is rain, and provision from earth is crops and fruit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r1.anchor: يعني النبات والثمر وإنما أمر أن يسأل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r2.claim: The question confronts idolaters with the fact that the sole acknowledged provider deserves worship, which is why the Prophet is told to answer that it is God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r2.anchor: وإنما أمر أن يسأل الكفار عن هذا احتجاجا عليهم بأن الذي يرزق هو المستحق للعبادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r3.claim: God is specified as the answer because the idolaters would give no other answer about who provides for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r3.anchor: ولهذا قيل له قل الله لأنهم لا يجيبون بغير هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r4.claim: The statement that God is the answer completes one sentence; the Prophet is then commanded to say the next statement to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r4.anchor: ولهذا قيل له قل الله لأنهم لا يجيبون بغير هذا وهاهنا تم الكلام ثم أمره أن يقول لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r5.claim: The majority of exegetes take aw as meaning wa, so the statement asserts that the Prophet's side is guided and the opponents are astray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r5.anchor: مذهب المفسرين أن أو هاهنا بمعنى الواو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda paraphrases the statement as saying that we are guided and you are plainly astray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة معنى الكلام وإنا لعلى هدى وإنكم لفي ضلال مبين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r7.claim: Al-Farra agrees that the meaning is effectively conjunction but rejects treating aw as grammatically equivalent to wa; it marks a delegated choice, as in taking one or two dirhams but not three.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r7.anchor: غير أن العربية على غير ذلك لا تكون أو بمنزلة الواو ولكنها تكون في الأمر المفوض كما تقول إن شئت فخذ درهما أو اثنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r8.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r8.claim: Al-Farra paraphrases the line as allowing either side to be described as lost or guided while the speaker knows his own side is guided and the other astray, making the accusation indirect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r8.anchor: وإنما معنى الآية وإنا لضالون أو مهتدون وإنكم أيضا لضالون أو مهتدون وهو يعلم أن رسوله المهتدي وأن غيره الضال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r9.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r9.claim: Al-Farra explains that Arabs soften a harsh curse or rebuke with a less direct substitute; examples include altering قاتله الله, جوعا, and ويحك, illustrating the verse's oblique wording.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p454/r9.anchor: ومن كلام العرب أن يقولوا قاتله الله ثم يستقبحونها فيقول قاتعه الله ويقول بعضهم كاتعه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r1.claim: God alone creates and provides, and is therefore alone in divinity: the polytheists admit that only God sends rain from heaven and grows crops from earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مقررا تفرده بالخلق والرزق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r2.claim: The formulation is wrap-and-spread: one party is rightly guided and the other plainly astray; it cannot be that both parties share guidance or error, and the proof of divine oneness exposes their polytheism.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r2.anchor: هذا من باب اللف والنشر، أي: واحد من الفريقين مبطل، والآخر محق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r3.claim: Qatada says Muhammad's companions told the polytheists that they were not both following one way and one of the two groups must be guided.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: قد قال ذلك أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم للمشركين: والله ما نحن وإياكم على أمر واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r4.speaker: عكرمة وزياد بن أبي مريم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r4.claim: Ikrima and Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam explain the meaning directly: we are guided and you are plainly astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة وزياد بن أبي مريم: معناه: إنا نحن لعلى هدى، وإنكم لفي ضلال مبين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to ask who provides, then answer for them that God provides; this assumes inward assent they may refuse to voice because stubbornness and love of idolatry silence them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r1.anchor: أمره بأن يقررهم بقوله : { من يرزقكم } ثم أمره بأن يتولى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r2.claim: They may withhold an admission that God provides because acknowledging it obliges them to worship the provider instead of powerless idols.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r2.anchor: لأن الذي تمكن في صدورهم من العناد وحب الشرك قد ألجم أفواههم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r3.claim: He compares this argument with Yunus, where the polytheists answer that God provides and are told that anything beyond truth is error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r3.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله : { قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r4.claim: He also links it to the question who is Lord of the heavens and earth, followed by the challenge of taking powerless patrons besides God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r4.anchor: ونحوه قوله عز وجل : { قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r5.claim: After compelling their admission, the Prophet frames the dispute fairly: one party among monotheists and idolaters must be guided and the other plainly astray.
