KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r5.anchor: ومعناه : وإن أحد الفريقين من الذين يوحدون الرازق من السموات والأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r6.claim: This even-handed formulation sounds fair to friend and opponent; the preceding questioning makes clear who is guided, while indirectness advances debate with less quarrel and gradually blunts resistance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r6.anchor: وهذا من الكلام المنصف الذي كل من سمعه من موال أو مناف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r7.claim: Indirect phrasing can win an argument more effectively and with less hostility, as in saying God knows which of two disputants is truthful and one must be lying.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r7.anchor: ونحوه قول الرجل لصاحبه : علم الله الصادق مني ومنك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r8.speaker: حسان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r8.claim: Hassan's verse illustrates the argument's fair but pointed, indirect form: of two opponents, the worse is sacrificed for the better.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p590#2/r8.anchor: ومنه بيت حسان : أتهجوه ولست له بكفء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r1.claim: على suits the guided person, pictured riding a fine horse above the way; في suits the misguided person, submerged and lost in darkness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r1.anchor: لأن صاحب الحق كأنه مستعل على فرس جواد يركضه حيث شاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r2.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r2.claim: Ubayy reads إما in place of أو, yielding either we or you are on guidance or in clear error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p591/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي : ( وإنا أو أياكم إما على هدى أو في ضلال مبين )

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r1.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r1.claim: Heavenly provision is rain and earthly provision is vegetation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن رزق السموات المطر ورزق الأرض النبات , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r2.claim: Alternatively, heaven's provision is what God decreed for servants, and earth's is what He enabled them to take as lawful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن رزق السموات ما قضاه من أرزاق عباده , ورزق الأرض ما مكنهم فيه من مباح

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r3.claim: “God” may be the polytheists' answer, since they did not deny that God provides for them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r3.anchor: أن يكون للمشركين حين سئلوا عن ذلك لأنهم لا يجحدون أن الله رازقهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r4.claim: Alternatively, they are ordered to answer “God” so their acknowledgment establishes proof against them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r4.anchor: أن يكون أمرا في أمر الله أي يجابوا به لأنهم لا يجحدونه لتقوم به الحجة عليهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r5.speaker: عكرمة وأبو عبيدة وزياد بن أبي مريم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r5.claim: One view means believers are guided and opponents are in manifest error.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r5.anchor: أحدها : معناه : إننا نحن لعلى هدى وإنكم أنتم لفي ضلال مبين , قاله عكرمة وأبو عبيدة وزياد بن أبي مريم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r6.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r6.claim: Al-Farra says “or” here has the force of “and.”

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r7.claim: The wording leaves open which side is guided, avoiding direct self-reproach or insult.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r7.anchor: إضافة للصدق إلى نفسه ودفعا عن صاحبه , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r8.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r8.claim: Al-Naqqash says God provides for both, while one group is guided and the other astray.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p449/r8.anchor: الثالث : معناه : الله رزقنا وإياكم لعلى هدى كنا أو في ضلال مبين حكاه النقاش

MUQATIL:34:24/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:24/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:24/r1.claim: The question addresses Meccan idolaters who worship angels: rain comes from heaven and plants from earth.
MUQATIL:34:24/r1.anchor: { قل } لكفار مكة الذي يعبدون الملائكة { من يرزقكم من السماوات } يعني المطر { والأرض } يعني النبات

MUQATIL:34:24/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:24/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:24/r2.claim: The Meccans answered Allah, with we are provided understood; the Prophet is told to say that God provides for you, then the speech breaks off.
MUQATIL:34:24/r2.anchor: يرزقنا إضمار، قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: { قل الله } يرزقكم

MUQATIL:34:24/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:24/r3.speaker: كفار مكة
MUQATIL:34:24/r3.claim: The Meccans proposed comparing worldly livelihoods and told Muhammad and his companions they were astray.
MUQATIL:34:24/r3.anchor: قال كفار مكة للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: تعالوا ننظر في معايشنا من أفضل دنيا

MUQATIL:34:24/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:24/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:24/r4.claim: Muhammad and his companions are the guided party, while the Meccan unbelievers are in manifest error; one of the two groups must be so.
MUQATIL:34:24/r4.anchor: إن أحد الفريقين لعلى هدى، يعنى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم نفسه وأصحابه

MUQATIL:34:24/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:24/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:24/r5.claim: The alif here is extra, as in the wording cited from 25:44.
MUQATIL:34:24/r5.anchor: الألف هاهنا صلة، مثل قوله عز وجل: { ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r1.claim: The Prophet asks who provides, then answers for them that God does: they inwardly admit it but refuse to say so because this entails worshipping the provider, not powerless idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r1.anchor: أمره بأن يقررهم بقوله من يرزقكم ثم أمره بأن يتولى الاجابة والاقرار عنهم بقوله يرزقكم الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r2.claim: Acknowledging that God provides exposes the inconsistency of worshipping beings unable to provide.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r2.anchor: لزمهم أن يقال لهم فمالكم لا تعبدون من يرزقكم وتؤثرون عليه من لا يقدر على الرزق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r3.claim: This fair-minded formulation says one faction, monotheists or polytheists, is guided and the other astray; even an opponent recognizes its fairness.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r3.anchor: وهذا من الكلام المنصف الذى كل من سمعه من موال أو مناف قال لمن خوطب به قد أنصفك صاحبك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r4.claim: The preceding proof subtly indicates which side is guided; indirectness better achieves the debater's aim.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r4.anchor: وفى درجة بعد تقدم ما قدم من التقرير دلالة غير خفية على من هومن الفريقين على الهدى ومن هو فى الضلال المبين ولكن التعريض أوصل بالمجادل إلى الغرض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r5.claim: Different prepositions picture the guided person riding a fine horse and the misguided person submerged in darkness, unable to see where to go.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p326#2/r5.anchor: لأن صاحب الهدى كانه مستعل على فرس

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r1.claim: Since idols own nothing of what God can do, Muhammad is told to ask who provides from heaven and earth: rain, sun, moon, stars and their benefits, and earthly water and plants. Idols cannot claim these works; if the polytheists admit God provides, they concede He alone should be worshipped.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r1.anchor: لما ذكر أن آلهتهم لا يملكون مثقال ذرة مما يقدر عليه الرب قرر ذلك فقال: قل يا محمد للمشركين

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r2.claim: The “either we or you” wording presents the case with apparent fairness, like saying one of us is lying while knowing oneself truthful; it indirectly declares the two camps opposed, with the Prophet's side guided and the polytheists astray.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r2.anchor: هذا على وجه الإنصاف في الحجة كما يقول القائل: أحدنا كاذب، وهو يعلم أنه صادق

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r3.claim: The two sides cannot share one position: one is guided and the other plainly astray; Qurtubi identifies the Prophet's side as guided and the polytheists as astray for associating partners with their provider.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r3.anchor: بل على أمرين متضادين، وأحد الفريقين مهتد وهو نحن والآخر ضال وهو أنتم

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r4.claim: “Iyyakum” coordinates with the subject of inna; coordinating to its syntactic position would instead give “aw antum.” Qurtubi says the first side alone is preferred for “upon guidance” in the former construction, though al-Mubarrad permits the first side in either analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r4.anchor: «أو إياكم» معطوف على اسم «إن» ولو عطف على الموضع لكان «أو أنتم»

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r5.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r5.claim: The Basran grammarians take “aw” in its ordinary disjunctive sense, not as doubt: Arabs use it this way when the speaker knows the answer but chooses not to state it.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r5.anchor: و«أو» عند البصريين على بابها وليست للشك، ولكنها على ما تستعمله العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Farra say “aw” means “and,” yielding: we are guided and you are in manifest error.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والفراء: هي بمعنى الواو، وتقديره: وإنا على هدى وإياكم في ضلال

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi glosses the preceding Jarir line as referring to Thalaba and Riyah.

QURTUBI-FULL:34:24#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:24#2/r2.claim: Qurtubi cites an unnamed poet's line, where “aw” joins Riyah and Rizam, as a further usage of the particle.
